title: Cold rebuild: Job execution order
summary: Rebuild Job execution order from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Job execution order** in *Real workflows: .NET and Docker*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Why is `if: always()` on the *test results* upload step?
options: When `dotnet test` fails, later steps are skipped by default, and failing runs are exactly when you need the report
So the artifact is never deleted
Because artifacts cannot be uploaded from successful runs
steps.explain: Steps after a failed step are skipped unless their `if` says otherwise.

steps.title: Rebuild Job execution order cold
prompt: Write `List<string> ExecutionOrder(Dictionary<string, List<string>> needs)` that returns one order in which the jobs could run one at a time.
`needs[job]` lists the jobs it waits for. Whenever several jobs are ready, run the one that comes first **alphabetically** (ordinal).
`{ build: [], lint: [], test: [build], docker: [build, test] }` → `build, lint, test, docker`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
